articles.title: CJI Surya Kant To Inaugurate India's First Victim Rights Centre At Patna On Sept 26
articles.content: CJI Surya Kant To Inaugurate Victim Rights Centre On Single Window System Model At Patna On Sept 26 By - LIVELAW NEWS NETWORK Update: 2026-09-24 07:16 GMT Image By: Siddharth Anand Click the Play button to listen to article The Chief Justice of India, Justice Surya Kant , will inaugurate the Victim Rights Centre at the Bihar State Legal Services Authority (BSLSA), Patna , on September 26, 2026 . On the same occasion, the Chief Justice will also launch a Transgender Helpline , flag off a fleet of Multi Utility Vehicles , and release a publication on the Centre. The Centre has been established as a pilot project under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 . Victims of crime often have to engage with multiple institutions, including police stations, hospitals, courts and government departments, each operating through separate procedures. Various rights and entitlements are available under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 , the Bihar Victim Compensation Scheme, 2014 , and allied laws, including emergency medical treatment, legal aid, copies of FIRs, participation in bail proceedings, compensation, protection measures and appellate remedies. However, support mechanisms are presently spread across District Legal Services Authorities, District Criminal Injuries Compensation Boards, police authorities, One Stop Centres, welfare departments, hospitals and non-governmental organisations. The Centre seeks to provide a single point of entry for victims, maintain a unified case record and function through prescribed internal timelines. Cases are to remain open until relief is obtained and verified or until closure is sought in writing. The project does not create a new statutory body and operates through existing infrastructure, personnel and coordination with police authorities, hospitals, Child Welfare Committees, One Stop Centres, State departments and organisations already working in the field. The Centre is intended to facilitate and monitor access to available rights and services and does not itself disburse compensation. It may be noted that the Kerala State Legal Services Authority is also operating a Victim Rights Centre under its legal services framework, albeit on a different model. The Bihar initiative seeks to introduce a single-window system through which victims can access and coordinate multiple entitlements and services from a single point of contact. The project has been developed under the guidance of Justice V. Kameswar Rao , Chief Justice of the Patna High Court and Patron-in-Chief of the Authority, and Justice Sudhir Singh , Judge of the Patna High Court and Executive Chairman of the Authority. Policy oversight is vested in a Steering Committee chaired by a Judge of the Patna High Court, with Justice Ajeet Kumar serving as its first Chairman. A Coordination Committee comprising representatives of relevant departments and agencies will oversee inter-departmental implementation, while administrative control rests with the Member Secretary of the Authority. Recognition Of 'Situational Victims' The Centre also proposes maintaining records relating to "situational victims". This category includes dependent family members of sole earning undertrial prisoners whose prolonged incarceration results in loss of income, disruption of education, delayed medical treatment and loss of property....

articles.title: Kandla–Thoothukudi Coastal Green Shipping Corridor set to get weekly container service
articles.content: Home Coastal Shipping Kandla–Thoothukudi Coastal Green Shipping Corridor set to get weekly container service Kandla–Thoothukudi Coastal Green Shipping Corridor set to get weekly container service September 24, 2026 News Category Coastal Shipping Container Shipping Green Shipping Ports Shipping Line GANDHIDHAM: India’ s first proposed Coastal Green Shipping Corridor between Kandla in Gujarat and V.O. Chidambaranar (VOC) Port in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, is set to receive a dedicated weekly container service, marking a significant step towards strengthening coastal cargo movement and promoting greener maritime transportation. The Indian Port Rail & Ropeway Corporation Ltd. (IPRCL) has invited shipping companies to operate the proposed service between Deendayal Port Authority (Kandla) and VOC Port Authority, Thoothukudi. The Kandla–Thoothukudi route was identified by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways ( MoPSW ) in 2025 as India’s first Coastal Green Shipping Corridor, to be developed in partnership with the Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) , Deendayal Port Authority and VOC Port Authority. The initiative envisages facilitating cleaner coastal maritime transport while supporting the development of green-fuel infrastructure along the corridor. Dedicated Two-Way Container Service Discussions between VOC Port and SCI in June 2025 had identified potential cargo flows in both directions. These included raw cotton and chemicals from Gujarat, along with solar panels, tyres and machinery spares from Tamil Nadu. Under the latest IPRCL tender, the selected operator will be responsible for arranging and operating dedicated vessels between Kandla and Thoothukudi and providing the return service to Kandla. The proposed operation will require two container vessels, each with a minimum capacity of 1,000 TEUs, to maintain a weekly sailing frequency. The estimated round-trip voyage between the two ports is approximately 14 days. Six-Month Initial Operation The service is proposed to commence initially for a period of six months, with the possibility of extension up to two years, depending on cargo availability, operational requirements and satisfactory performance. IPRCL has estimated the project cost at approximately ₹150 crore. The selected shipping company will undertake the complete operational management of the service, including vessel and crew arrangements, scheduling and voyage management, bunker procurement, port agency coordination, and payment of port dues and marine service charges. The operator will also coordinate cargo and terminal activities, including loading and unloading operations, commercial management of vessel slots and monitoring of cargo movement. In addition, the selected company will work closely with customers and other stakeholders to generate cargo bookings and facilitate efficient movement of containers along the corridor. Advancing Green Coastal Shipping The proposed weekly service is expected to strengthen the maritime link between India’s western and southern coasts while creating a structured coastal route for two-way containerised cargo movement. The initiative also forms part of the broader effort to develop green shipping corridors in India, combining regular coastal connectivity with the gradual adoption of cleaner fuels and supporting infrastructure. articles.title: Jay Meena wins India's first Asian Games soft tennis bronze, credits coaches and government
articles.content: ANI Photo | Jay Meena wins India’s first Asian Games soft tennis bronze, credits coaches and government Indian soft tennis player Jay Meena made history by securing the country’s first-ever Asian Games medal in the sport, winning bronze in the men’s singles event at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. Meena’s campaign concluded in the semi-finals where he was defeated by Japan’s Takuya Kurosaka in a 2-4 set contest. After losing the first three sets, Meena fought back to take the fourth and fifth sets, narrowing the margin to 2-3 before Kurosaka won the sixth set 4-1 to seal victory. The final scoreline was 3-5, 1-4, 1-4, 4-1, 6-4, 1-4, as reported by ESPN. Add TNM on Google He had previously guaranteed a historic podium finish for India by defeating Sherwin Nuguit of the Philippines in the quarter-finals, ensuring a medal as all semi-finalists were assured of a place on the podium. Speaking after his bronze medal win, Meena described his journey at the Games as a “rollercoaster”, citing setbacks such as losses in the quarter-finals against Indonesia and in mixed doubles matches. He said, “Our team went through many ups and downs. On September 18, when we played the quarterfinals against Indonesia, that was a medal-winning match, but we lost. It was a deeply heartbreaking moment. After that, on September 20, we also had chances in the mixed doubles, but we lost again. So, to make a comeback from there and pull off this medal… I am very happy. I would like to give full credit to my coach, the Amateur Soft Tennis Federation of India, and especially, to SAI (Sports Authority of India) and the central government.” ADVERTISEMENT Meena also highlighted challenges faced by Indian athletes due to dietary restrictions as vegetarians. He noted the lack of dedicated Indian cuisine options at international competitions and said, “No one prepares special food separately for one particular country, whether it’s the Asian Games or the Olympics. Therefore, it would be much better if an Indian chef were sent along with the team so that we could at least eat fresh food. We have to survive on food with preservatives.” He described his diet during the Games as relying on ready-to-eat meals, theplas (a type of traditional Indian bread), salads, and corn. “We bring ready-to-eat meals with us. We reconstitute the ready-to-eat vegetables, which contain preservatives, by mixing hot water into them. Then there are theplas that last for 30 days—we have to eat those for vegetarian options. And I would also like to say that we got through many dinners and mornings just on salad and corn. I ate a lot of corn here,” Meena said. articles.title: NTPC terminates 400 MWh Mouda BESS contract - Renewable Watch
articles.content: NTPC Limited has terminated the contract awarded to GR Infraprojects Limited (GRIL) for a 400 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) project at Mouda Super Thermal Power Station in Maharashtra. The contract, awarded in March 2026 at a total value of Rs 4.13 billion, was scheduled for completion within 15 months. According to the official release, the project faced delays in critical activities, and GRIL failed to achieve the required progress despite a contractual notice from NTPC seeking corrective action. NTPC has terminated the contract and encashed securities of approximately Rs 910 million in accordance with the contractual provisions. Additionally, NTPC has initiated the process to re-tender the project at GRIL’s risk and cost. NTPC is taking steps to facilitate the early re-award and implementation of the project. Earlier this month, NTPC Renewable Energy Limited invited bids for the supply and installation of wind turbine generators for an interstate transmission system-connected wind project with a nominal capacity of 600 MW. The project is located in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, and will comprise 200 WTGs. thermal power battery energy storage Maharashtra Energy GR Infraprojects NTPC Renewable Energy Energy storage BESS
